items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I was with Lunceford and we heard this guitar player... Ray Nance was the guy who encouraged me to go with Lunceford... I didn't experiment a whole lot when I went with Lunceford

ctx.x: When did -- you were in Tommy Miles' Band in what year?

It must have been '31, '32 -- '31, '30 because I went with Earl Hines right after that. Jimmy Mundy was the first guy to go with Earl Hines. But I'll tell you how this kind of came about. We used to play a battle of music all the time with a band from Baltimore, and this band was called the Ambassadors.

Now, in this band there was a trumpet player, high note trumpet player. He was very flashy, and his name was Stevenson. But he went with Lunceford later on. He was the first high note trumpet player that Lunceford had before Paul Webster was Stevenson. He went with -- Tommy was a fantastic trumpet player. Played a lot of high

items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: the first movie I did was with Lincelford in about '38, and this was that "Blues in the Night" movie

ctx.x: the first thing I did with Louis, and then we did "High Society", and the next one we did was the Red Nichols story of Five Pennies. And then he did something else, "The Beat Generation". It was a sad -- was a bad movie. I don't know what it was about. And he did something like that.

But those were the ones I did with him over there. Of course, the first movie I did was with Lincelford in about '38, and this was that "Blues in the Night" movie with Jack -- what's his name? Was it Jack Carson? I think it was Jack Carson. It's way back.
I've seen references to it, but I don't really know. It was a feature-length movie, right?
